source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 14. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

learn.en: Allah told the angels He would place a khalīfah on the earth. The angels asked why; Allah said: “I know what you do not know.” (Qur'an 2:30)
learn.title: The announcement

learn.en: Allah taught Adam the names of all things. The angels said: “Glory be to You! We know only what You taught us.” Adam told them the names. (Qur'an 2:31–33)
learn.title: Honoured with knowledge

learn.en: Allah told the angels to bow to Adam to honour him. All did — except Iblīs, who refused out of pride. (Qur'an 2:34)
learn.title: Iblīs's pride

learn.en: Adam and his wife lived in the Garden and could eat anything except from one tree. Shayṭān whispered, and they ate from it. (Qur'an 20:120–121)
learn.title: The tree

learn.en: They said sorry: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be losers.” (Qur'an 7:23) Allah forgave Adam, and he became the first prophet on earth.
learn.title: Saying sorry to Allah

quiz.en: Why did Iblīs refuse to bow?
True or false? Allah forgave Adam when he said sorry.
True or false? Shayṭān is our friend.

think.q: When you make a mistake, what can you learn from Adam?
think.a: Don't be proud like Iblīs — say sorry to Allah and to people, and try again.

parents.summary: Allah honoured Adam with knowledge. Iblīs refused out of pride. Adam slipped, said sorry, and Allah forgave him — the door of tawbah is always open.
parents.tip: Teach your child that saying “sorry” quickly is what prophets do.
